summary.headline: Bondada guides FY27 revenue growth of 60-70% on a INR7,147 crore order book; FY26 revenue reported at INR2,843 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of about INR2,843 crore (vs INR1,571 crore in FY25) and a net profit of about INR211 crore, with the order book at INR7,147 crore as of 31 March 2026. Q4 EBITDA margin dipped on low-margin billing and higher steel and cable prices, which management says is not structural; FY26 margin rose about 30 bps to 7.5% from 7.2%. Cash from operations was positive at INR125 crore after collections above INR1,000 crore in Q4. New initiatives in BESS, data centres, defence and an IPP of 2 GW in Andhra Pradesh were highlighted as FY27 drivers.

segments.name: Renewable energy EPC
segments.commentary: Largest order book segment at INR4,536 crore (about 65% of total). About 1.3 GW commissioned cumulatively; about 0.5 GW commissioned in FY26 and target of about 1.5 GW in FY27, taking cumulative to about 3 GW.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Order book INR1,463 crore covering about 850 MW from Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. Tamil Nadu 400 MWh due in about one year (financially closed, Canara Bank funding); AP 450 MWh due in about 18 months, financial closure pending.

segments.name: Telecom (BSNL)
segments.commentary: About 1,536 BSNL towers installed and about 1,506 on-air (about 99% strike rate). Management is pursuing Kavach railway passive-infrastructure tenders, with first win from South Central Railway.

segments.name: Services / O&M
segments.commentary: Management said O&M rose from about INR90 crore to about INR140 crore in FY26. An analyst's reading of a segment drop from about INR356 crore to INR140 crore was disputed; management said it would recheck the segmental reporting.

segments.name: Products and defence
segments.commentary: Products are targeted to rise from about 10% to 30% of mix (EPC 90% to 70%). First defence order is a missile component (BEL, about INR4 crore per analyst) with execution in about three months.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: One assignment under way in Hyderabad, with a second data centre in Vizag. Management expects 7-8% of FY27 revenue and EBITDA of 14-15%; no long-term capex planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 60-70% expected, with order book of about INR7,150 crore to be executed over 18-20 months.
Net profit growth of about 60-70% in absolute terms (analyst reading: 50-60% on bottom line); management said margins should be maintained.
EBITDA margin for FY27 to be flat or up 20-30 bps; Q1 margins expected to hold since materials were procured in advance.
Target 1.5 GW of solar EPC commissioning in FY27 and 7.8 GW portfolio to be commissioned over 2-2.5 years.
Vision 2030: 25 GW of renewable capacity (16 GW solar, 9 GW BESS) and about USD 1 billion revenue.
Migration to main board of BSE and NSE planned in FY27.
capex_capacity: Integrated manufacturing plant on about 27 acres near Hyderabad: capex INR120-130 crore including land; construction to start in Q2 FY27 with about one-year build time; incremental revenue expected from FY28.

AP 2 GW IPP via SPV, with about INR9,000 crore order value excluded from the INR7,147 crore order book; phased build of 250 MW first, then 500 MW tranches, full 2 GW by 2030, revenue from 2031; first 250 MW needs about INR250 crore equity.
GreenBond RE Park IPP targets 2 GW; IPP IRR expected about 17-18% for solar and 12-13% for BESS BOO projects.
Adani EPC order (about INR1,050 crore) at about 20% completion with plant to be commissioned by March 2027; management said it is slightly ahead of schedule.
demand_pricing: Tender participation of INR25,000-30,000 crore with a 20-25% win rate; about INR2,850 crore of L1 orders expected to convert in Q1 FY27.
Company stayed out of reverse auctions on some BESS tenders it considered unviable; it lost NTPC BESS tenders on price.
Receivable collections from NLC, NTPC, Singareni and MAHAGENCO with working capital of 85-90 days; PSU collection risk not seen.
Cable prices rose about 17-18% in the last quarter of FY26; steel also rose, with the increase seen as seasonal plus geopolitical. Some contracts are pass-through and some fixed.
Data-centre capex per MW of INR35-40 crore of company scope; starting size 2-3 MW, scalable to 10 MW.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and profit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 60-70% revenue growth on the INR7,150 crore order book, with profit growing about 60-70% in absolute terms; an analyst's reading of 50-60% for the bottom line was not corrected.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 margin dip and whether FY27 margin of 11-12% EBITDA and 7% PAT is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip was attributed to low-margin billing in Q4 and higher steel and cable costs; the CMD said 11-12% EBITDA and about 7% PAT were achievable comfortably.

qa_highlights.question: Equity needs and funding for the 2 GW AP IPP?
qa_highlights.answer: Phased equity of about INR250 crore for the first 250 MW; the rest to be raised in tranches. Management said it has funding avenues and no immediate QIP plan was stated.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the company not part of recent NTPC and Coal India BESS tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recent BESS tenders were largely unviable; it bid in some NTPC tenders but was not L1, and stopped at reverse-auction thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre margins and revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres are expected to be 7-8% of FY27 revenue at EBITDA of 14-15%; the company will not hold long-term capex and aims to hand over shells and infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Segmental services revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said O&M rose to about INR140 crore from INR90 crore and that some services had been reclassified into EPC; it said it would recheck the segment disclosure.

risks_watch: Segmental reporting inconsistency: services revenue figures in the quarterly disclosure were questioned and management committed to recheck.
Raw material inflation (steel, cables) and geopolitical effects on petroleum-linked inputs; Q1 FY27 margin guidance depends on procurement lock-in.
Working capital: current liabilities up sharply on TReDS and advances; receivables about 27-28% of revenue, aging 87 days, with some items over one year.
Execution risk: 1.5 GW commissioning target in FY27 and the Adani order commissioning by March 2027.
Funding and dilution for the 2 GW AP IPP and the AP BESS project financial closure, which was still pending.
Defence entry depends on trials of the missile component and on inorganic deals for three companies still in advanced talks.
Track L1 conversion of INR2,850 crore in Q1 FY27 and the Bryanston data-centre assignment.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on order book, growth and new segments, but defensive on the Q4 margin dip, segmental reporting questions and BESS pricing details, which were deferred to one-on-one meetings. Several answers were inconsistent or contradictory on figures (EBITDA, revenue guidance), which lowers confidence in the precision of guidance.
key_quotes: So having said this, maybe anything around 60% to 70% of revenue growth will be there even coming financial year.
We're making it ready and then giving back to the hyperscalers. So we are not going to sit on any Capex in long term.
EBITDA margins for this year will remain same or maybe we will have a little improved margins of by about 20, 30 basis points yes.
